question: Which of the following novels of Shashi Tharoor is a satirical verse on the epic Mahabharata?

options.text: The Hindu Way: An Introduction to Hinduism

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Great Indian Novel**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Great Indian Novel"** by Shashi Tharoor is a satirical and allegorical reimagining of the Indian epic **Mahabharata**. 
 
• The novel cleverly weaves India's history, politics, and independence movement into the framework of the Mahabharata, blending mythology with modern events.
 
• **The title itself is a pun on the phrase "The Great Indian Epic."**
 
• Characters and events from the Mahabharata are reinterpreted to represent political figures and incidents from India's struggle for freedom and post-independence era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Why I Am A Hindu**

 
 
• A non-fiction work that explores the philosophy, beliefs, and diversity of Hinduism, along with Tharoor's personal connection to the religion.
 
 
 
• **The Hindu Way: An Introduction to Hinduism**
 
 
• This book provides a deeper understanding of Hinduism, its traditions, practices, and relevance in contemporary times.
 
 
 
• **Tharoorosaurus**
 
 
• A playful collection of essays showcasing Tharoor's linguistic flair and love for the English language, explaining uncommon words with wit and humor.
